reviews.one: Driven by record FII inflows exceeding ₹1.1 lakh crore and robust domestic macroeconomic upgrades, Indian equities hit milestone highs even as global markets reeled from AI valuation shocks and hawkish Fed rate hike pressures.
reviews.html:
What moved markets

  • Record FII Inflows: Foreign portfolio investors pumped over ₹1.1 to ₹1.22 lakh crore into Indian equities through November, propelling the Nifty toward 26,000 and the Nifty Bank past 64,000.
  • Global Tech & AI Sell-off: Nvidia board turmoil, Anthropic’s volatile Nasdaq debut, and global AI valuation skepticism triggered the worst global equity week since 2020.
  • Hawkish Fed & US Dollar Strength: Markets priced in a near-100% probability of a December Fed rate hike, strengthening the U.S. dollar and driving a sharp freefall in global bullion (gold at 14-month lows) and industrial metals.
  • Strong Domestic Macro Prints: October core sector growth surged to a 13-month high of 10.9%, and agencies like Moody's and ADB raised India's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7.0%.
  • Domestic Inflation & Currency Pressures: Retail inflation touched 6.1% (breaching the RBI’s tolerance band), while a surging rupee past 93/USD sparked margin concerns for export-heavy IT services.

Stories that developed during the week

  • Banking Sector Momentum & Governance Shocks:
  • Initial report (Mon-Tue): Public sector banks posted record H1 FY27 net profits of ₹1.1 lakh crore, and Nifty Bank rallied to record highs above 62,000 on robust FII inflows and credit demand.
  • Evolution (Wed-Sun): While Nifty Bank crossed 64,000, the sector faced severe governance and regulatory jolts, including IndusInd Bank terminating its former/current CEO over derivatives accounting lapses, PNB estimating a ₹5,000 crore ECL provisioning requirement, and gold-loan NBFCs facing margin squeezes.
  • Global Commodity & Metal Slump:
  • Initial report (Mon-Wed): Broad-based global corrections in crude, precious metals, and industrial metals began creating inventory loss and margin concerns for domestic manufacturing and cable firms.
  • Evolution (Thu-Sun): The slump deepened into a severe multi-day rout—with gold down 37% and silver down 65% from peak levels—weighing heavily on metal producers and gold-backed lenders despite relief from lower input costs in consumer durables.
  • Aviation & Corporate Distress (SpiceJet):
  • Initial report (Wed): SpiceJet’s board approved a ₹5,500 crore fundraise and planned to file overdue financial results, offering initial upward momentum.
  • Evolution (Thu-Fri): The story deteriorated as the airline faced severe cash crunches, cancelled over 70% of its flights, and received a 7-day DGCA show-cause notice amid heavy operational disruptions.
  • Regulatory Interventions & Quick-Commerce Compliance:
  • Initial report (Mon-Tue): SEBI reviewed norms to simplify IPOs and raise FPI beneficial ownership thresholds while weighing margin trading leverage limits.
  • Evolution (Wed-Sun): Regulatory tightening expanded across sectors as SEBI rolled out faster IPO execution frameworks, IRDAI proposed insurance distribution fee caps, and FDA license suspensions hit dark stores of major quick-commerce players (Amazon, BigBasket, Zepto, Blinkit) across Maharashtra.

Sectors: who gained, who lost

  • Gained:
  • Banking & Financial Services: Surged to record highs (Nifty Bank >64,000) on massive FII inflows, robust credit expansion, and strong PSB profitability.
  • Power & Utilities: Benefited from strong core sector growth, evening power deficit tailwinds (boosting thermal players like NTPC and Coal India), and aggressive renewable energy expansions.
  • Hospitals & Healthcare: Outperformed the broader market, driven by capacity additions and strong institutional upgrades (e.g., Apollo Hospitals hitting record highs).
  • Textiles & Apparel: Gained from double-digit export growth and potential order diversions from regional operational disruptions.
  • Lost:
  • Metals & Mining: Suffered severe headwinds from the global commodity crash, plunging copper and bullion prices, and low-cost Chinese steel imports.
  • Aviation & Logistics: Pressured by soaring fuel costs, fare demand dips, and severe operational distress at carriers like SpiceJet.
  • Traditional IT Services: Faced ongoing AI-driven pricing pressures and earnings headwinds from sharp rupee appreciation.
  • Quick-Commerce & Retail Deliveries: Hit by sudden regulatory crackdowns and FDA license suspensions across dark stores.

Into next week

  • Watch for monthly F&O contract expiry and market closures on November 24 for Guru Nanak Jayanti.
  • Track the subscription finalization and market debut of Mahanadi Coalfields' ₹8,981 crore IPO.
  • Monitor incoming U.S. macroeconomic cues and global crude oil price action ahead of the impending December Federal Reserve rate decision.
  • Look for further developments regarding India-EU Free Trade Agreement negotiations ahead of the expected December 16 signing.

reviews.one: Indian benchmarks rallied past Nifty 25,000 on record FII inflows (>₹84,000 crore) and global upgrades, shrugging off severe global tech shocks before high domestic CPI inflation (6.09%) brought late-week consolidation.
reviews.html:
What moved markets

  • Massive Foreign Inflows & Global Upgrades: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FIIs) executed a dramatic pivot into India, pouring over ₹84,291 crore into domestic equities in the first half of November. Major global brokerages—including HSBC, Goldman Sachs, and Standard Chartered—upgraded Indian equities to 'overweight', driving benchmarks to multi-month highs and pushing India's market valuation to $5.4 trillion.
  • Domestic CPI Breaches RBI Ceiling: October retail inflation spiked to a two-year high of 6.09%, breaching the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper tolerance limit. This sparked fears of a 25 bps repo rate hike in December, causing 10-year G-Sec yields to harden to ~7.31% and capping late-week market momentum.
  • Global Tech Volatility & Leadership Shocks: Global tech sentiment was hit by an internal governance probe into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which subsequently culminated in his sudden resignation and wiped out hundreds of billions in market cap worldwide.
  • Crude Oil Moderation: Brent crude plunged nearly 6% early in the week toward the $90–$91/bbl mark as geopolitical supply risks eased, relieving domestic macro pressure and import costs.
  • MSCI Index Rejig: MSCI added Coforge, LIC, Adani Green, and Meesho to its global index, generating an estimated $2 billion in passive inflows for domestic markets.

Stories that developed during the week

  • Nvidia Governance Crisis & Global Tech Shock:
  • Early Week: Nvidia shares plunged 8–9% following an internal board investigation into CEO Jensen Huang regarding conduct and an affair linked to a Chinese spy.
  • Mid-to-Late Week: Sentiments worsened despite solid earnings from alternative cloud play CoreWeave. By Friday/Saturday, Huang’s official, sudden resignation erased hundreds of billions in global tech value, driving rotation out of AI proxies.
  • India Macro & Inflation Dynamics:
  • Early Week: Easing crude oil ($90–$97/bbl) and strong capex/credit growth projections (Q2 GDP estimated at ~7.8%) set a bullish macro backdrop.
  • Late Week: Inflation printed at 6.09% for October—breaching the 6.0% ceiling for the ninth consecutive month. Hardening domestic bond yields (7.31%) and expanding trade deficits ($39.9 billion) shifted market focus back to potential RBI rate hikes.
  • Automotive Sector Divergence:
  • Mid-Week: Data showed record-breaking October festive passenger vehicle sales (5.19 lakh units, up 16.1% YoY in two-wheelers).
  • Late Week: Operational divergence emerged—while Ashok Leyland reported record revenues and ABB/Hitachi reported strong order inflows, Tata Motors posted a net loss of ₹5,531 crore due to JLR restructuring charges, and Ola Electric shares tanked on revenue declines.
  • Fintech & Regulatory Approvals:
  • Late Week: Regulatory overhangs eased significantly for key fintech players as Paytm received preliminary RBI approval for its prepaid/wallet license (driving its stock to record highs) and Razorpay cleared SEBI hurdles for its $600 million IPO.

Sectors: who gained, who lost

  • Gained:
  • Banking & Financials / NBFCs: Driven by accelerating credit growth (19%–21% YoY), strong Q2 profits (~20% YoY growth), and major capital raises (Bajaj Finance's ₹11,700 crore QIP). PSU banks saw strong momentum early in the week.
  • Capital Goods & Power Infrastructure: Outperformed on order wins and execution beats (Hitachi Energy, TD Power, ABB India) alongside government approvals for a ₹68,800 crore renewable power corridor.
  • Real Estate: Outperformed with multi-month high surges, buoyed by H2 launch pipelines, joint development agreements, and institutional investments.
  • Oil & Gas / Refiners: Benefited from early-week drops in global crude oil prices, boosting refining and marketing margins.
  • Lost / Underperformed:
  • IT & Global Tech Proxies: Weighed down by global tech governance shocks, Nvidia's collapse, and cautious revenue/headcount outlooks.
  • Consumer Durables & Apparel: Squeezed by margin pressures and cost inflation, highlighted by sharp drops in Whirlpool of India (net profit down ~40%) and Page Industries (margins narrowing).
  • Automobiles (Select OEM & EV plays): Despite record festive dispatches, Tata Motors (JLR restructuring losses) and Ola Electric (Q2 revenue down 39%) dragged down overall segment sentiment.

Into next week

  • Primary Market Activity: Over ₹10,000 crore to be raised, led by Coal India subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields launching its mega ₹9,500 crore IPO on November 19.
  • Macro & Yield Watch: Market direction will hinge on how benchmark 10-year G-Sec yields (7.31%) and US Treasuries adjust to rate-hike threats following domestic CPI (6.09%) and US PPI prints.
  • Trade Deal Progress: Tracking final-stage US-India bilateral trade negotiations, where India is working to secure lower preferential tariffs relative to Asian peers.
  • FII Inflow Persistence: Monitoring whether foreign institutional buying continues its strong pace after the massive ₹84,290 crore surge in the first half of the month.

reviews.one: India decoupled from the global tech sell-off, riding historic FPI inflows and a ~17–19% plunge in crude prices to close Samvat 2082 and kick off Samvat 2083 above the Nifty 25,000 mark.
reviews.html:
What moved markets

  • Historic FPI Inflows: Foreign portfolio investors pumped over ₹45,970 crore ($4.11+ billion) into Indian equities over five sessions, driving the strongest weekly gain since February 2021 and overpowering past year-long sell-offs.
  • Crude Oil Tailwind: Brent crude suffered its biggest weekly drop since 2020 (~17% to 19% decline) as Middle East war premiums faded, providing a massive macro cushion for India's import bill and current account.
  • Robust Domestic Macro Fundamentals: India's growth narrative was reinforced by an IMF/RBI FY27 growth forecast upgrade to ~7%, alongside October GST collections surging 22.9% year-on-year to ₹2.31 lakh crore.
  • US Midterm Clarity vs. Global Yields: While a Democratic sweep in the US midterms eased trade and visa concerns, surging US Treasury yields and reviving Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations (72%-80% probability) stoked global volatility.
  • Q2 Earnings & Festive Resilience: Markets navigated mixed corporate earnings divergence alongside a late-week festive recovery, anchored by strong Dhanteras deliveries and record EV adoption despite initial headline auto retail dips.

Stories that developed during the week

  • Crude Oil & Oil-Linked Sectors: Initially reported midweek as a sharp ~19% decline driven by easing Middle East tensions, the crude narrative evolved by the weekend into managing extreme volatility and West Asian freight risks—prompting strategic shifts like IOC acquiring its own shipping fleet while continuously boosting OMCs and paint manufacturers.
  • Automobile Retail Demand vs. Wholesale Dispatches: The story began with FADA reporting a headline 23% drop in October retail auto sales due to festive calendar shifts and dealer inventory costs, but evolved positively as single-day Dhanteras deliveries, robust SUV demand, and a 93.6% surge in passenger EV registrations salvaged the November retail outlook.
  • Foreign Capital Rotation & Market Milestones: Starting the week marked by historic FPI selling across Samvat 2082, the narrative dramatically inverted as India emerged as a preferred hedge against global AI/tech sell-offs, resulting in record weekly inflows that pushed Nifty past 25,000 and set a high-water mark for domestic market capitalization ($5.31 trillion).

Sectors: who gained, who lost

  • Gained:
  • Banking & Financials: Outperformed on robust Q2 earnings, strong credit growth, and private bank strength (e.g., ICICI Bank, NBFC gold loans).
  • Oil & Gas: Benefited directly from plunging Brent crude prices lowering input and import costs for OMCs.
  • Metals & Mining: Bolstered by strong Q2 earnings beats and margin expansions from majors like Tata Steel.
  • Lost:
  • Cement, Capital Goods & FMCG: Grappled with severe margin compression due to rising raw material, power, freight, and input cost inflation (e.g., Thermax, Coromandel).
  • Telecom & Select IT: Weighed down by rising network expansion costs, shortening deal tenures, and corporate AI budget caps (e.g., Bharti Airtel Q3 misses).

Into next week

  • Monitor domestic retail inflation (CPI) data, which is projected to touch a 24-month high of 6.1%, threatening the RBI's threshold.
  • Track the sustainability of FPI inflows and post-Muhurat profit-booking trends following the sharp weekly market rally.
  • Watch the RBI's scheduled meeting with banks on November 12 regarding the implementation of the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework.
  • Keep an eye on upcoming corporate dividend record dates (CONCOR, HUDCO, NBCC, RITES) and prominent stock lock-in expiries between November 9–13.
